extracted.intended_audience: U.S.-based early career researchers (untenured, tenure-track assistant/associate professors), full-time employees at DOE national laboratories and Office of Science user facilities, and university/lab research administrators preparing applications
extracted.subtask_short: DOE Early Career Research Program application
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and submit a mandatory pre-application (and, if invited, a full application) for the U.S. Department of Energy Office of Science Early Career Research Program FY2024, ensuring eligibility, alignment with DOE program priorities, and adherence to stated deadlines and award-request guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant employment/status eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for the program, a researcher must be an untenured, tenure-track assistant or associate professor at a U.S. academic institution or a full-time employee at a DOE national laboratory or Office of Science user facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit gatekeeping eligibility requirement; applicants must hold one of the listed positions at the time of application. Institutions outside these categories are not specified as eligible employers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility window / career-stage timing
rubrics_metrics.description: For a second year the Office of Science is extending the eligibility window for this competition from 10 to 12 years for all applicants to address special circumstances and challenges due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should verify their years-since-terminal-degree fall within the extended 12-year window; this extension applies broadly to all applicants for this competition year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible recipient organizations and awardee type
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards will support researchers at U.S. academic institutions, DOE national laboratories, and Office of Science user facilities; awards to an institution of higher education and awards to DOE national laboratories/user facilities are treated differently in funding requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be affiliated with one of the specified organization types because award contracts/payments are made to the institution. Confirm institutional eligibility and award routing (university vs lab/user facility) before preparing the requested budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amounts and project duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards to an institution of higher education will be approximately $875,000 over five years and the minimum request for awards to a DOE national laboratory or Office of Science user facility will be approximately $2,750,000 over five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget requests should be consistent with these approximate totals and the five-year project duration; labs/user facilities should plan for substantially larger minimum requests than higher-education institutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted research topics and program office selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Early career researchers may apply to one of eight Office of Science program offices: Advanced Scientific Computing Research; Biological and Environmental Research; Basic Energy Sciences; Fusion Energy Sciences; High Energy Physics; Nuclear Physics; Accelerator R&D and Production; and Isotope R&D and Production. Proposed research topics must fall within the programmatic priorities of DOE’s Office of Science as provided in the program announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must select the single appropriate program office and ensure their proposed research aligns with that office’s programmatic priorities (see the program announcement for detailed priorities). Topic alignment is a required constraint for admissibility and competitive review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application process: mandatory pre-application and invitation to submit full application
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-applications are mandatory and are due on Tuesday, January 30, 2024, at 5:00 p.m. ET. Only those applicants that receive notification from DOE encouraging a formal application may submit full applications. Full applications (by invitation) will be due on Thursday, April 25, 2024, at 11:59 p.m. ET.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the mandatory pre-application by the stated deadline—failure to submit a pre-application or to receive DOE encouragement disqualifies applicants from submitting a full application. Track notification timelines closely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and evaluation mechanism: competitive peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding will be competitively awarded on the basis of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare materials (pre-application and full application, if invited) with peer review criteria in mind: clarity of significance, approach, innovation, investigator qualifications, and alignment with DOE priorities (details are in the program announcement). Expect review by subject-matter peers and competitive ranking among applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program scale and intended impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The program will support over 80 early career researchers for five years to allow scientists to push the frontiers of knowledge and, as needed, gain experience working across large scientific facilities at the department’s national laboratories and user facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize how the proposed work advances major scientific challenges and leverages (or will gain experience with) DOE national laboratory or user facility capabilities where appropriate; the program prioritizes high-impact early-career research and facility engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant resources and informational events
rubrics_metrics.description: A webinar on this opportunity will be held on January 10, 2024, at 1:00 p.m. ET; further information can be found on the Office of Science funding opportunities page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend the webinar and consult the Office of Science funding opportunities page and the formal program announcement for detailed instructions, application forms, program priorities, and any Q&A or clarifications prior to submission.
